songs.name: THE ICE CREAM TRUCK STILL PLAYS ITS SONG
songs.sub: A new song, THE ICE CREAM TRUCK STILL PLAYS ITS SONG: an ice cream truck parked on a cul-de-sac in Summerlin, its battery dying, its jingle still calling kids who left with their families. Its own lead, a music box, the truck's own jingle, its own drums (a footstep for the kick, a bottle breaking for the snare, a kid slurping for the hat), in G lydian. It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

what.1: 1. THE MAP: the song as it plays on the map, the tune on top, a soft 120 beat under it.
what.2: 2. THEIR TURN: tension. The tune stays, the chord is held, the kick on the beat, the bass pushing.
what.3: 3. YOUR TURN: everything, much louder: the tune doubled an octave, the full kit, the bass driving, a hit when the turn comes back to you.

songs.name: THE WEDDING CHAPEL TAKES ONE MORE BOOKING
songs.sub: A new song, THE WEDDING CHAPEL TAKES ONE MORE BOOKING: a drive-through wedding chapel on the Strip with its lights on and its organ playing, booking couples who never come. Its own lead, a pump organ, the chapel's own, its own drums (the chapel door knocked for the kick, a champagne glass breaking for the snare, a sip for the hat), in G harmonic minor. It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: THE LOUNGE SINGER STILL TAKES REQUESTS
songs.sub: A new song, THE LOUNGE SINGER STILL TAKES REQUESTS: the lounge of a dead casino where a voice still sings to empty tables, taking requests from nobody. Its own lead, an ondes martenot, a voice that is not a voice, its own drums (a soft footstep for the kick, a breath for the brush, a saw stroke for the ride, swung), in B flat dorian. It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: ONE SIGN IN THE BONEYARD STILL BUZZES
songs.sub: A new song, ONE SIGN IN THE BONEYARD STILL BUZZES: the field off Las Vegas Boulevard where the dead signs were laid down, and one tube that still lights at night. Its own lead, a vibraphone, cold metal, its own drums (a footstep for the kick, a neon tube breaking for the snare, a crackle for the hat, half time), in E minor pentatonic. It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: LAKE MEAD GIVES BACK WHAT IT TOOK
songs.sub: A new song, LAKE MEAD GIVES BACK WHAT IT TOOK: the reservoir going down year after year, a town's roofs coming up out of the water, and the barrels on the new shore. Its own lead, a bamboo flute you can hear the breath in, its own drums (a drop of water for the kick, a boat's wood creaking for the snare, another drop for the hat), in A hirajoshi (five notes). It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: THE MONORAIL RUNS WITH NOBODY ON IT
songs.sub: A new song, THE MONORAIL RUNS WITH NOBODY ON IT: the Strip's monorail still running its loop on the last power, the doors opening at every empty station. Its own lead, a clarinet, the old-world kind, its own drums (a train for the kick, a crow on the rail for the snare, the train's rattle for the hat), in F sharp phrygian dominant. It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: THE MOTEL SIGN SAYS VACANCY
songs.sub: A new song, THE MOTEL SIGN SAYS VACANCY: a motel on Fremont whose VACANCY sign has never once gone off, every room open, every key on its hook. Its own lead, a lap steel guitar, sliding, its own drums (a boot heel for the kick, a bottle breaking for the snare, a saw stroke for the shaker, a gallop), in D dorian. It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: THE WATER TOWER READS OUT NUMBERS
songs.sub: A new song, THE WATER TOWER READS OUT NUMBERS: the water tower in North Las Vegas whose old emergency speaker plays a tune at night and then reads out numbers. Its own lead, a whistled tone, the station's call sign, its own drums (a low snore for the kick, a cough on the microphone for the snare, a breath for the hat, the tresillo), in B in-scale (five notes). It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: THE BUFFET STILL LAYS OUT THE TRAYS
songs.sub: A new song, THE BUFFET STILL LAYS OUT THE TRAYS: an all-you-can-eat buffet off the Strip that still sets out its trays every evening, and the line that still forms for them. Its own lead, an accordion, a polka at the end of the world, its own drums (a grunt for the kick, a laugh from the line for the snare, a breath for the hat, oom-pah), in C sharp harmonic minor. It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: THE IMPERSONATOR DOES TWO SHOWS A NIGHT
songs.sub: A new song, THE IMPERSONATOR DOES TWO SHOWS A NIGHT: a man in a white jumpsuit who still does both his shows in a showroom with the power out, to applause from the dark. Its own lead, a twangy electric guitar, the old rock and roll kind, its own drums (a footstep for the kick, the audience clapping for the snare, a drink poured for the hat, swung), in E flat mixolydian. It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.

songs.name: THE HOSPITAL KEEPS ONE LIGHT ON
songs.sub: A new song, THE HOSPITAL KEEPS ONE LIGHT ON: the hospital on Charleston with one window lit on the fourth floor every night, a monitor still beeping for someone. Its own lead, a celesta, a lullaby on a ward, its own drums (a soft footstep for the kick, a cough on the ward for the snare, a ventilator's breath for the hat, the heartbeat), in C minor (aeolian). It plays in the game now, in turn with the others.
